name: Validator, auditor or attestor
oneLine: Re-execution, zkML or TEE attestation, reputation services.
goals: Produce an independent score for an agent's work that others can read on chain.
Verify that an agent's claimed output came from the claimed model and inputs, by re-execution, a zkML proof or a TEE quote.
Build a reputation service that filters Sybil feedback and weights reviews by proof of payment.
Attest to agent identity and behavior in a format that merchants, facilitators and controls platforms can consume.
Get paid for validation work through the same rails the agents use.
pains: The ERC-8004 Validation Registry is specified but not officially deployed, so validation lives in community registries with no shared address.
LLM outputs are not deterministic, so re-execution does not reproduce results and cannot prove misbehavior.
zkML is slow and expensive for real models, and TEE attestation depends on hardware vendors and quote verification.
Most feedback on chain comes from coordinated Sybil reviewers, so aggregate scores are not usable without heavy filtering.
requestHash squatting and mutable registration files weaken the link between a validation and the agent it describes.
decisions: Which validation method to offer: re-execution, zkML, TEE attestation, or statistical sampling.
Which trusted-client lists and proof-of-payment rules to apply when computing a summary.
Whether to write results to an on-chain registry, an off-chain API, or both.
What soft and hard finality mean for a validation response, and when to update it.
